messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selection tweak we see a consistent perf regression on long-context workloads. Captured an nsys trace (attached) showing sustained HBM bandwidth spikes and repeated KV read hotspots around the same timeline.

kyle: Oof. Do you have a short timeline snippet? Is it during generation or during KV population?

maria: generation. root cause looks like read-amplification in the KV layer when seq_len >= 3072. From the nsys summary: 
```
Time(ms)  Kernel                               Calls  Total(ms)  Avg(ms)  HBM-GB/s
1200      fused_attention_forward              48     450.2      9.38     120.5
1215      kv_cache_read_span                    376    310.8      0.83     280.9  <-- repeated microbursts
1236      cuBLAS_sgemm                         96     210.4      2.19     95.8
```
Note the kv_cache_read_span entries map to a small kernel that issues many small reads; together they saturate HBM and push attention kernels into noisy tails.

cheng: That pattern smells like suboptimal prefetch stride + small microbatches. When KV pages are misaligned, we get read storms that cause eviction waves. Any perfetto flamegraph around 1214-1220?

maria: Yes — perfetto shows bursts of memcpy + page faults synced with the read_span spikes. Sequence-length distribution for the repro job: 512 (10%), 2048 (30%), 3072-4096 (60%). Problem amplifies as the long tails hit.

ash: Two quick experiments to try: 1) increase KV page size from 64KB -> 256KB in the runtime config to reduce the number of GV-read ops, 2) enable stride-based prefetch with stride=4 so sequential KV lookups prewarm adjacent pages. Both are low-risk and cheap to A/B.

kyle: Also try coarsening batching heuristics: switch to adaptive microbatching that merges requests when expected remaining tokens <= 32. That reduces repeated small KV reads across calls.

maria: Agreed. I ran a short A/B locally: enabling stride-prefetch cut KV-read call count by ~48% and reduced observed HBM bandwidth from ~580GB/s to ~360GB/s on the NSYS capture window. However latency variance increased slightly for short sequences (p95 +12ms).

ci-bot: perf/regression: model-gen-longseq: baseline p95=225ms, new p95=249ms (+10.7%); cost/tokens baseline=0.71c, new=0.64c (-9.9%). See artifact: ci://run/2070011/trace

cheng: Tradeoff expected — less bandwidth at the cost of a bit more latency for short sequences. We should target a dynamic policy: enable stride-prefetch only when avg_seq_len in the window > 1024. Also consider adaptive page sizing per-device.

ash: For KV eviction waves, a practical mitigation is a soft-LRU that pins recent KV pages for long sequences and evicts cold tails more aggressively. Might be more invasive but worth prototyping.

maria: Next steps: (1) kyle to run a perfetto capture with and without stride-prefetch on dedicated node (ticket #ENG-rl-412), (2) cheng to prototype dynamic prefetch gating based on rolling seq_len histogram, (3) ash to add a telemetry gauge for "kv_read_ops_per_sec" and HBM instantaneous sample to Console dashboards. I'll collect nsys/perfetto links in the ticket.

kyle: On it. I'll include capture commands in the ticket: 
```bash
# reproduce workload
nsys profile -o /tmp/kvprefetch --trace=cuda,cublas,osrt --sample=cpu --cpuctrl --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi 
# perfetto (deferred) - record for 60s during regen window
perfetto --config my.cfg --out /tmp/kvprefetto.pftrace
```

ash: I'll add the metrics and a quick alert when kv_read_ops_per_sec spikes > 2000 sustained over 5s.

maria: Thanks all — moving the thread to the eng-runtime ticket and attaching the traces. Will update after the AB runs. :thumbsup:
